original.note: Yes. Wave 1's contract is Setup and Mother Ship/assurance-2026-10-05/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md lines 23-56: the five required ids at line 29, and H4's default native homes at line 50. Those ids are in the gate's -v output and the named homes are private. The findings are holes that text does not close.

findings.message: private_account_path treats as private only the isolated provider-accounts store, Path.home() joined with NATIVE_HOME_DIRS (.claude, .codex, .grok, .gemini), and the CODEX_HOME / CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / GROK_HOME redirects (provider_native.py:44-45 and 70-73). A live call of that function returned False for Path.home()/'.claude.json', Path.home()/'.config'/'claude'/'credentials.json', and Path.home()/'.agy'/'settings.json'. share_onboard.py:476-487 already lists those as Claude and Gemini login/session markers. report_viewer.resolve_project_artifact (report_viewer.py:401-417) then read_bytes() any in-project file the guard does not mark private, and GET /artifact/ is AUTH_OPEN (route_table.py:164), so a registered project folder that encloses the home — the precondition test_h4 uses — serves those files with no cookie. The same false result lets handle_project_file_content (anchor_gui.py:19938-19939) and the deliverable-file route (steward_cockpit/steward_routes.py:991-992) through. The green proofs plant only .codex/auth.json, .claude/.credentials.json, .grok, CODEX_HOME, and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (tests/test_provider_setup_rigor.py:761, tests/test_provider_setup_hardening.py:414).

The login worker checks cancel only before the follow-up refresh (provider_setup.py:346-348). login_status(cancel=True) still sets the cancel event and state cancelling while the record is awaiting_browser (provider_setup.py:381-383), and that is still the record's state for the whole refresh. refresh swallows NativeError, so a cancel during the read never reaches the except at line 362. Lines 350-359 then set state completed when auth is signed_in or the observation has error, and the finally at line 369 overwrites cancelling. A cancel that arrives after native login returns and during the status read is reported as a completed sign-in, including the H6 case where the status read itself failed. test_h6 never cancels, and test_r2a cancels while the stand-in is still inside login, so this window stays green.

The five required ids are present and the H1-H6 bodies now pass because the fixes are in the product code; that is the post-fix proof, not an unimplemented wave.

findings.message: The Cave and Desk capacity rail still builds its single Claude row from latest_limit_signal(now, j) with no connection id (usage_capacity.py:278). The account filter at usage_capacity.py:128-137 runs only when connection_id is not None, so the newest job log wins, including another connection's qualified log or a legacy unqualified log. The row note still says two accounts cannot be told apart (usage_capacity.py:255-256). anchor_gui._high_seat_context and the Desk both publish that row (anchor_gui.py:7899 and anchor_gui.py:8175). separate-account-allowance-attribution proves ProviderService.snapshot and latest_limit_signal(connection_id=...) only. The browser half of failure-keeps-existing-session-and-quality replaces the seat context capacity with an empty list (tests/test_provider_setup_rigor.py:630), so the green gate never renders this rail.

repro.command: python -c "import inspect, usage_capacity; src=inspect.getsource(usage_capacity.anchor_seen); assert 'latest_limit_signal(now, j)' in src"
